title: New Zealand Inflation Eases in Q3
body: New Zealand's annual inflation rate eased to 3.7% in the third quarter of 2026, down from 4.1% in the previous quarter and slightly below market expectations of 3.8%. Despite this moderation, inflation remains above the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's 1–3% target range. Petrol was the single largest contributor to annual inflation, surging 19.1% amid higher international oil and fuel prices linked to conflict in the Middle East. The cost of building new homes rose 3.2%, reflecting increased material, subcontractor, labour, and fuel costs. Electricity prices climbed 9.3%, international airfares were up 12.5%, and local authority rates and payments increased 6.2%. These rates, which are measured annually in the September quarter, have been a significant driver of inflation in recent years. On a quarterly basis, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.7%, a marked slowdown from the 1.5% increase recorded in the second quarter. title: New Zealand CPI Cools to 3.7% in Q3 2026, Easing from 4.1% YoY

The latest data, updated on 21 October 2026, indicate a gradual cooling in price pressures compared with the same period a year earlier. The figures reflect a year-over-year comparison, where the current 3.7% reading measures the change in prices in the third quarter of 2026 versus the third quarter of 2025. The previous 4.1% figure was calculated on the same basis, comparing the second quarter of 2026 to the second quarter of 2025. The steady deceleration from Q2 to Q3 suggests that inflationary pressures, while still present, are easing over time. Market participants and policymakers are likely to scrutinize subsequent data releases to assess whether this moderation in price growth will continue and what it could mean for the broader economic outlook and future policy decisions. title: Argentina's EMAE Contracts for Second Straight Month
body: Argentina's economic activity contracted by 1.7% year-on-year in August 2026, deepening from a 1.4% decline in July and defying expectations for a 0.3% increase. Of the 15 sectors surveyed, 10 registered declines, with fishing recording the sharpest drop at 15.7%. Manufacturing output fell 3.2%, while wholesale and retail trade and repair activities decreased 3.5%. Financial intermediation shrank 3.8%, transport and communications were down 2.9%, and tax-related revenues declined 4.2%. By contrast, five sectors posted annual growth. Mining and quarrying led the gains, expanding 11.1%, followed by electricity, gas and water, which rose 4.3%, and hotels and restaurants, up 3.1%. On a month-on-month basis, the EMAE (Monthly Estimator of Economic Activity) edged up 0.1% in seasonally adjusted terms, partially recovering from a 2.9% drop in July. title: Ibovespa Falls as Election Uncertainty Weighs
body: The Ibovespa declined 0.9% on Wednesday, closing at 206,495 amid mounting electoral uncertainty. The index opened higher but reversed direction after a Quaest poll showed challenger Flávio Bolsonaro and incumbent President Lula virtually tied in the presidential runoff. The survey also indicated that 52% of respondents would "never" vote for Bolsonaro, versus 47% for Lula, whose rejection rate dropped six percentage points in a week. Despite the lack of detailed policy proposals from Bolsonaro, investors see his candidacy as more likely to deliver fiscal reforms that could support lower interest rates. This backdrop weighed on credit-sensitive stocks, with most financial names retreating. Bradesco edged down, Banco do Brasil slipped 0.4%, Itaúsa fell 0.6%, and B3 reversed earlier gains to close 0.8% lower. Retailers also traded mostly in negative territory, led by a 3.4% drop in Magazine Luiza. In other corporate moves, WEG sank 7.3% after reporting weaker-than-expected third-quarter margins. title: Canadian Stocks Gain as Oil Rally Eases
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index climbed 0.6% to close at 36,325 on Wednesday, supported by easing pressure on credit‑sensitive stocks as oil prices remained volatile. Crude trading was choppy ahead of next week's Bank of Canada policy decision, and a pause in the recent oil rally provided some relief for major banks, which have been under strain from persistent inflation concerns and elevated borrowing costs. RBC gained 1.2%, TD Bank advanced 2%, BMO added 1.7%, and Scotiabank rose 1.6%. Despite the respite, markets largely expect the BoC to raise interest rates at next week's meeting, with additional policy clarity anticipated when the federal budget is released on November 5. In resources, most mining names moved higher as gold prices inched up, lifting Barrick by 0.6% and Franco‑Nevada by 0.9%. The technology sector also firmed: Shopify ticked up 0.4%, while Celestica gained 1.4%, tracking a rebound in US AI hardware stocks following strong results from SpaceX. title: Brent Tops $109 Amid Escalating Middle East Tensions
body: Brent crude climbed back above $109 a barrel on Wednesday, erasing earlier losses in a turbulent session as attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure intensified across the Middle East. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said naval mines had forced three tankers to halt after they attempted to use routes Tehran considers unauthorized, while the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that a vessel had been struck near Oman. Despite mounting security risks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said shipments through the Strait of Hormuz were nearing prewar levels, and data from Kpler and Vortexa indicated that overall Middle Eastern exports have risen since the summer. Separately, Yemen's Houthi militants claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the Shaybah oilfield, as well as on airports in Riyadh and Abha. US EIA data showed crude inventories declined by just over 3 million barrels last week, undershooting the 4.9 million-barrel draw reported in industry figures. title: Oil Wavers Below $98 as Supply Recovers
body: Crude oil prices slipped back below $98 a barrel on Wednesday after briefly touching $100 in a highly volatile trading session. The market is coming under pressure from rising crude exports out of the Middle East, where producers have stepped up shuttle shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman. Tanker-tracking data show that seaborne flows from the region have now exceeded pre-war levels. Saudi Arabia's crude exports climbed 7.9% in August, reaching their highest level since March. At the same time, Russia is preparing to send its first diesel cargo to the United States on Thursday under an agreement between Presidents Trump and Putin. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington is also exploring cooperation with India's Reliance Industries to refine Western energy supplies. Nonetheless, geopolitical tensions across the Middle East remain elevated, and record-high freight rates in the Persian Gulf continue to lend support to crude prices, limiting the extent of the recent pullback. title: US Stocks Rise on Tech Gains
body: US equity markets finished higher on Wednesday, supported by renewed optimism over AI-related demand following strong corporate results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer. The S&P 500 advanced 0.6%, the Nasdaq climbed 1.1%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 360 points. SpaceX shares jumped 7.8% after Elon Musk said a merger with Tesla would be "a good idea," and the company reported its first profit as a public entity. Tesla gained 3.4%, and the positive sentiment extended to other space-related names, including Rocket Lab (+5.4%), Planet Labs (+2.3%), and Intuitive Machines (+3.5%). Super Micro Computer soared 9.5% after issuing a robust quarterly outlook, which helped lift other hardware names such as Hewlett Packard Enterprise (+3.7%) and Dell (+5.3%). Semiconductor stocks also advanced, with Nvidia up 2.5%, Intel gaining 1.3%, and AMD rising 3.4%. On the downside, Netflix dropped 5.3% after providing a weaker-than-expected profit forecast for the fourth quarter, just days after announcing workforce reductions. AT&T fell 6.4% despite beating earnings estimates, and Elevance Health declined 1.4% even as it raised its profit outlook for 2026. title: U.S. 20-Year Bond Auction Yield Rises to 5.469%, Marking Uptick in Long-Term Borrowing Costs
body: The yield on the United States 20-year Treasury bond climbed at the latest auction, with the indicator ending at 5.469% on 21 October 2026, up from the previous level of 5.420%. This rise in the 20-year yield underscores shifting conditions in the long end of the Treasury market, where even small changes in auction results can reflect evolving investor expectations for interest rates, inflation, and fiscal dynamics. The higher yield may indicate that investors are demanding slightly more compensation to hold longer-dated U.S. debt compared with the prior auction.
